item.title: Thinkmine introduced the Kobo programming language for .NET
item.description:
Thinkmine has released the general-purpose programming language Kobo for the .NET ecosystem in preview. Developers link the language's emergence to the spread of agent development and code generation based on specifications. The project is focused on collaborative development by humans and AI agents and is currently in its early stages, so the syntax may still change. The authors formulated four design principles: native AI support, declaration consistency, reliance on a ready-made runtime, and self-documentation. Instead of third-party libraries for working with models, developers have added language constructs for prompts and tools. Read more

item.title: Russian ModernBERT: Pre-training and Post-training
item.description:
Hello, Habr! My name is Anton Kabaev, Technical Lead at the Center for Natural Language Processing, MWS AI. In this article, we will describe how we trained two ModernBERT models for the Russian language. A Russian-language encoder can be trained from scratch, or you can take a pre-trained multilingual model and replace its vocabulary. We tried both approaches. BERT is an encoder language model. It converts text into vectors, which can be used to classify texts, find similar phrases, or rank documents. During BERT training, some tokens are masked. In the sentence 'The train departs from the [MASK] platform,' the model must restore the gap using words to the left and right. Through many such examples, the encoder learns language patterns and facts about the world. This is pre-training. But what happens if you change the exercise for an already trained encoder and continue training it? We created two Russian-language ModernBERT models of different sizes. We trained the Small model with approximately 35 million parameters from scratch, and obtained the Base model from the multilingual mmBERT. For comparison, we took open-source models from a Russian developer of the same size, RuModernBERT-small and RuModernBERT-base. We tried post-training on both of our models and on the ready-made base model from the Russian developer. It was this one that benefited the most: the average accuracy on seven RussianSuperGLUE tasks increased from 70.88% to 74.12%. We will explain how the encoders were trained, what changed after post-training, and why the choice of model depends on how you intend to use it. Read more

item.title: Skills over MCP: The MCP server now sends skills with it
item.description:
On November 24th, Anthropic launched the public beta of Skills over MCP in Claude and Claude Code. The MCP server now serves skills automatically, eliminating the need for manual installation. I migrated two of my servers and analyzed logs: in November, they rejected around 4,400 server/discover requests, including those from Claude Code, even before the official announcement. Below, I detail the necessary server changes and how to test your setup with a single curl command.

item.title: In Russia, they proposed creating a system for independent verification of trusted AI
item.description:
Business proposed allowing independent laboratories to test AI systems in testbeds, i.e., in special environments. This will help customers and information system owners assess the possible risks of using neural networks and make a decision on implementation. If the AI system passes the test, is capable of performing certain tasks, and complies with security requirements, it acquires the status of trusted. This is stated in the draft concept of trust in AI systems. Vedomosti familiarized themselves with the project, its authenticity was confirmed by two sources: one in an IT company, the second in the Ministry of Digital Development. Read more

item.title: Citibank allows clients to use AI agents at their own risk
item.description:
Citibank, the third-largest commercial bank in the US, has updated its terms of service. According to the changes, clients using AI agents will be responsible for resolving any problems caused by them, even if it involves hacking. "As third-party AI tools become more accessible, it is important for customers to understand the associated risks. Customers who grant third-party AI agents access to their accounts are fully responsible for any actions taken through these agents," a bank representative told TechCrunch. Read more

item.title: How I'm learning English with Claude
item.description:
Still dreaming of a well-paying remote job, I decided to brush up on my English. I wanted to improve my vocabulary, conversational English, and grammar simultaneously. Hiring a tutor is expensive and requires scheduling. So, I started looking into various apps and websites. Given the rapid development of LLMs and their potential usefulness, I specifically sought out AI-powered services. I tried a total of 8 services (3 mobile apps, 4 websites, and 1 Telegram bot) and purchased three subscriptions, using trials for the rest. All these resources had cool features that, in my opinion, weren't always relevant and I have no idea who used them, but none of them fully met my needs. As a result, I decided to create my own language learning tool with Claude for Claude. If you're interested in what I came up with, welcome under the cut!

item.title: Why Employees Bypass Corporate AI, How to Change It, and Whether It's Worth It
item.description:
A company launches a corporate AI tool to help employees work faster. A couple of months later, it turns out it's barely used: employees still go to external chatbots and pay for personal subscriptions to solve work tasks. It seems intentional – work gets done with AI – but it's not certain that sensitive information isn't leaking to external systems. Find out what works instead of prohibitions.

item.title: OpenAI found a bug in GPT-6.2 limits. It worked for users for a week
item.description:
For a whole week, the error gave subscribers extra requests, and OpenAI found it themselves. On November 26, Thibault Sotiaux, who is responsible for Codex at the company, admitted that since the launch of GPT-6.2, the consumption of Astra and Sol in subscriptions was counted with a discount that should not have been there. The counter has already been fixed, so limits will now run out noticeably faster. Read more

item.title: "Zombie UI": Why Major Brands Are Releasing Interfaces That Are Embarrassing to Show
item.description:
Screenshots of interfaces generated by neural networks from major brands raise a logical question: have companies with billion-dollar budgets run out of designers and testers? Unfortunately, in many cases, this is not far from the truth. The problem isn't that AI 'can't' draw buttons. The problem is that the interface production process has been rebuilt around AI capabilities, not user needs. Read more
